text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some simple best practices. First, use clear endpoints that describe resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Third, provide good documentation so other developers can understand how to use your API easily. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can update your API without breaking existing applications. These rules make your API easier to use, maintain, and improve over time.
